Summary

I've successfully modified the preprocessing script to implement stratified train/test splitting with an 80:20 default split. Here are the changes:

Files Modified:

  1. preprocessing.py:

    • Added train_test_split import from sklearn.model_selection
    • Added split_ratio=0.8 parameter to process_and_save()
    • Added stratified split after data creation using random_state=42 for reproducibility
    • Saves separate :train and :test files with a split attribute

  2. config.py:

    • Added SPLIT_RATIO = 0.8 configuration (default 80:20)

  3. run_preprocessing.py:

    • Added -r/--ratio command-line argument to override the split ratio

How to use:

# Default 80:20 split
python run_preprocessing.py

# Custom split ratio (e.g., 90:10)
python run_preprocessing.py -r 0.9

# Test mode with mock data
python run_preprocessing.py -t

The stratified split ensures each user's samples are proportionally represented in both train and test sets, eliminating bias that could occur with random splitting.
